title: Exponentials and logarithms
learner: Returning learners who recall powers or log buttons but need to recover multiplicative models, inverse meaning, domain reasoning, and engineering ratio interpretation.
assumedKnowledge: F01 fractions, powers, exact arithmetic, and scientific notation
F02 equations, factoring, and interval domains
F03 function transformations and inverse reasoning

include: Exponential and logarithmic meaning and graphs
Discrete and continuous growth/decay, fitting, threshold times
Decibel intuition with explicit references and power relationships
exclude: Exponential regression algorithms or statistical model selection
Logistic models and general differential-equation solving
Acoustic exposure guidance, RF system design, or unsupplied circuit relationships

routes.quick: Use five diagnostic probes, follow the specific lesson recommendation, read Quick recall, and attempt each independent checkpoint. Finish the four-question mixed recall after all five objectives.
routes.full: Study the five lessons in sequence. Work reasoned examples, guided tasks, prediction activities, and varied practice before independent checkpoints. Use notes to split longer lessons across sessions.

escalation.text: MTH 215 is the full-course destination. Its m05 module is planned in this baseline, so the verified free OpenStax sections supply fuller first-time instruction in the meantime.

overlap: MTH 215 b02 and F01 cover integer exponent rules and exact notation.
MTH 215 m05-l01 through m05-l04 are planned; no authored lessons or exponential/logarithmic generators were found.
F03 supplies general domain, transformation, and inverse reasoning but its graph-parent union does not include exponential or logarithmic parents.
reuse.implementation: Wrap only mth-exponent-rules as f05-exponent-rules for the first lesson. Retain source IDs and saved attempts. Use rational/interval/root graders and choice-plus-numeric answers for nonrational logarithmic results; do not add a new general expression parser or change persistence.

coverage.probe: invalid log rule or discarded root

assessment.checkpoints: Four required independent questions per lesson, with multiple related fields where necessary. All objective questions are critical.
assessment.mixed: Four required questions: foundations combines a targeted exponential part and logarithm part; the other questions target rules/equations, models, and decibels. Keep each multipart question at eight fields or fewer and preserve p1/p2 field-level lesson targets.
assessment.evidence: Familiarity, visits, diagnostic work, and guided predictions never count as mastery. Reuse existing independent evidence, versioned attempts, notes, resume, and backup APIs. Retain misses until a successful independent lesson check.

sharedCapabilities.interface: Lesson.interaction adds { kind: 'refresher-explog-lab', mode: 'growth' | 'inverse' | 'rules' | 'decay' | 'decibels', prompt: string }.
sharedCapabilities.reason: These models need logarithm-domain checks, inverse-point comparisons, and threshold/ratio predictions beyond the existing graph parents.
sharedCapabilities.integration: One strict union member and one reader dispatch. Keep pure bounded model utilities and the activity implementation in refresher-owned files. Reuse QuestionFields and existing graders. No app-shell, storage, or backup changes.

verification: Independently verify exact powers and ratios, exp/log inverse identities, domains and graph asymptotes for both signs and bases above/below one.
Sweep meaningful variants with deterministic 100-seed checks, strict notation rendering, equivalent exact responses, domain-invalid input, and correct finite numeric tolerances.
Check equation completeness using an independent polynomial or inverse formulation and substitution in every original log argument.
Verify growth/decay fits and threshold times through independent ratios and exponentiation; include zero rate, zero target, initial target, past-only target, and dimensional consistency.

Verify decibel ratios by inverse exponentiation and supplied power laws, including negative levels, zero/negative quantities, resistance mismatch, cascades versus linear power sums, and reference changes.

Browser-test every checkpoint and mixed review, diagnostic routing, assisted versus independent evidence, all five guided activities, invalid/retry paths, reload/resume, notes, backups, keyboard use, mobile layouts, and Axe.
Run unit tests, lint, typecheck, and production build before preview availability. Independent human review remains pending.
Finish and verify F05 before planning F06.
